bib.title: Analyzing Multi-Head Self-Attention: Specialized Heads Do the Heavy Lifting, the Rest Can Be Pruned
bib.venue: ACL 2019 (Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, pp. 5797-5808)

question: How much does each encoder attention head of a translation Transformer contribute, do important heads play interpretable roles, and how many heads can be pruned without hurting BLEU?
hypothesis: The encoder may disambiguate the syntactic structure of the source sentence, so some heads should track syntactic relations; and most heads are redundant.
contributions: Identify important encoder heads with layer-wise relevance propagation and characterise their roles (positional, syntactic, rare words)
A head-pruning method using stochastic gates and a differentiable relaxation of the L0 penalty (Hard Concrete)
Show most heads can be pruned with small BLEU loss and that specialised heads are pruned last

method.summary: Transformer-base NMT models are trained from English to Russian, German and French. Heads are ranked by LRP relevance and confidence, their roles are measured against CoreNLP dependency parses, and per-head Hard Concrete gates with an L0-relaxation penalty prune heads while fine-tuning from the converged model.
method.task: neural machine translation (EN-RU, EN-DE, EN-FR); head analysis and pruning

datasets.name: WMT (EN-RU, EN-DE, EN-FR)
datasets.split: 50k English sentences from WMT EN-FR data not used in training are held out for the head analysis of Section 5.2
datasets.source: WMT; 2.5m matches EN-RU parallel data excluding UN and Paracrawl
datasets.preprocessing: BPE, source and target vocabularies of about 32000 tokens; batched by approximate sequence length

datasets.name: OpenSubtitles2018 (EN-RU)
datasets.preprocessing: only sentence pairs with relative time overlap of subtitle frames of at least 0.9 kept

models.name: Transformer base (encoder-decoder NMT)
models.architecture: encoder-decoder Transformer; heads gated in encoder only, or in all attention types
models.init_from: pruned models start from the converged unpruned model; 'from scratch' comparison uses random init
models.heads: h = 8 per attention sub-layer (48 encoder heads; 48 decoder self; 48 decoder-encoder)

other.dropout_etc: regularization as in Vaswani et al. 2017 (values not restated)

training.objective: cross-entropy + lambda * L_C(phi), L_C = sum_i (1 - P(g_i=0|phi_i)) with Hard Concrete gates, for pruning; plain cross-entropy for baselines
training.lr: lrate = scale * min(step_num^-0.5, step_num * warmup_steps^-1.5), scale = 4
training.lr_schedule: inverse square root after warmup (Vaswani et al. 2017)
training.regularisation: as in Vaswani et al. 2017 (not restated); L0 relaxation on head gates for pruning

other.pruning: gates resampled per batch; decoder fixed during encoder-only pruning (only encoder parameters and gates are fine-tuned); lambda varied to get different head counts (values not given); at test time gates set to 0 or 1 by the larger of P(g=0), P(g=1)
other.footnote8: fine-tuning a trained model gave 0.2-0.6 BLEU more than the regularised objective from scratch or a from-scratch model with the same heads

parameters.head_positional_threshold: max attention at one relative position >= 90% of the time
parameters.head_syntactic_threshold: accuracy at least 10% above best fixed relative-position baseline
parameters.confidence: average max attention weight excluding EOS

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: translation BLEU on the test sets (set not named)

metrics.name: LRP head relevance
metrics.definition: relevance of a head's neurons to the top-1 predicted logit, normalised over heads in a layer, averaged over all generation steps of a dev set

metrics.name: Head confidence
metrics.definition: average of the head's maximum attention weight excluding EOS, over tokens of dev sentences

metrics.name: Dependency accuracy
metrics.definition: how often a head's max attention (excluding EOS) lands on a token in the given CoreNLP dependency relation, in either direction, counted per relation and direction

baselines: Most frequent relative position per dependency relation (positional baseline)
Models trained from scratch with the same head configuration as pruned models
eval.protocol: Single trained models per setting as far as stated; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported. Syntactic analysis uses CoreNLP parses of held-out sentences.

evidence.quote: Each training batch contained a set of translation pairs containing approximately 1600010 source to- kens.
evidence.where: Appendix B.1 (the 10 is a footnote marker)

results.claim: Pruning 38 of 48 encoder heads on EN-RU WMT costs only 0.15 BLEU
results.setup: EN-RU WMT 2.5m, encoder-only gates, fine-tuned from converged model, 10 heads left
results.quote: pruning 38 out of 48 encoder heads results in a drop of only 0.15 BLEU

results.claim: On OpenSubtitles, pruning all but 4 of 48 encoder heads loses only 0.25 BLEU
results.quote: we lose only 0.25 BLEU when we prune all but 4 heads out of 48

results.claim: Pruning with gates in all attention types: the 14/31/30 head model keeps WMT BLEU
results.setup: EN-RU WMT 2.5m, heads encoder/decoder-self/decoder-encoder 14/31/30, pruned from trained model
results.table: Table 2, WMT row sparse heads 14/31/30, column BLEU from trained

results.claim: Training the sparse architecture from scratch is worse than pruning: 5/9/12 heads gives 28.90 pruned vs 28.41 scratch
results.table: Table 2, WMT row sparse heads 5/9/12, column BLEU from scratch

results.claim: OpenSubtitles 6/9/13 heads: pruned 32.27 vs 31.84 from scratch vs 32.4 baseline
results.setup: EN-RU OpenSubtitles 6m, 6/9/13 heads, pruned from trained model
results.table: Table 2, OpenSubtitles row sparse heads 6/9/13, column BLEU from trained

results.claim: Positional heads put at least 90% of max attention on one relative position, and their average max attention weight exceeds 0.8
results.setup: all positional heads in EN-RU, EN-DE, EN-FR
results.quote: the average maximum attention weight ex- ceeds 0.8 for every positional head for all language pairs considered here

results.claim: Best dobj head (verb to object) reaches 78% on WMT against a 41% positional baseline
results.table: Table 1, row dobj v->o, column WMT best head / baseline 78 / 41

results.claim: Best nsubj head (s to v) on OpenSubtitles reaches 70% against 45% baseline; v to s 77 / 45
results.table: Table 1, row nsubj s->v, column OpenSubtitles 70 / 45

results.claim: Rare-words head in layer 1 (OpenSubtitles) points to the rarest token in 66% of cases where the rarest token is outside the top-500
results.setup: OpenSubtitles models; sentences whose least frequent token is not in the top-500 most frequent
results.quote: this head points to the rarest token in 66% of cases, and to one of the two least frequent tokens in 83% of cases

results.claim: A model with 17 of 48 encoder heads retains heads with all identified functions
results.quote: the model with 17 heads re- tains heads with all the functions that we identiﬁed

results.claim: Encoder self-attention heads are pruned first; decoder-encoder attention heads are the most important
results.setup: EN-RU, WMT and OpenSubtitles, gates on all attention types
results.quote: the model prefers to prune encoder self-attention heads ﬁrst, while decoder-encoder attention heads appear to be the most important

results.claim: Gated models converge to nearly binary gates: open or closed
results.quote: the model converges to solutions where gates are either almost completely closed

limits: Only English-to-{Russian,German,French} translation with a Transformer-base encoder-decoder; no encoder-only or decoder-only language models.
Syntactic roles are tested for four dependency relations only, using CoreNLP parses as ground truth.
Authors cannot draw strong conclusions on the effect of target-language morphology; the subject-verb difference between domains is a hypothesis left to future work.
BLEU only; no variance, seeds or significance tests; test sets not named in the text; training steps, hardware and lambda values not stated.
Pruning compared to other compression methods is left for future work.
From-scratch training of the sparse architecture degrades, so the pruning finding is about trained models.

terms.definition: the average of its maximum attention weight excluding the end of sentence symbol, taken over tokens in a development set
at least 90% of the time its maximum attention weight is assigned to a specific relative position (in practice -1 or +1)
its accuracy on a dependency relation is at least 10% higher than the baseline that looks at the most frequent relative position

code.snippet: MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat_i(g_i * head_i) W^O ; L(theta, phi) = L_xent(theta, phi) + lambda * L_C(phi)
